Latin word

potestās

potestās, potestātis f.

noun, third declension

the power or possibility of doing something; power, control; the chance (to do something), leave; the chance, the opportunity (to do something)

In this lexicon

  • ability

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. potestās: “ability, power of doing any thing (class.)”

  • control

    also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 6.4: ut sit in senātūs populīque Rōmānī potestāte (Lewis & Short); Traupman 150; Traupman 296

  • opportunity

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 10.13.1: ut prīmum potestās data est augendae dignitātis tuae; Traupman 95, 289: mihi nōn potestātem dedit respondendī, he didn’t give me a chance to answer

  • possibility

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 10.13.1: ut prīmum potestās data est

  • Ipsa scientia potestās est.: knowledge is power

    modern

  • tribūnicia potestās: tribune

    classical

Examples

  • ut prīmum potestās data est augendae dignitātis tuae, nihil praetermīsī in tē ōrnandō

    as soon as I had the chance to add to your standing, I left nothing undone to honour youCic. Fam. 10.13.1
